input.quote: Section 7.1 No Resignation. The Servicer will not resign as Servicer under this Agreement unless it determines it is legally unable to perform its obligations under this Agreement.
input.rationale: The Agreement runs until the last Receivable is paid in full or the Issuer is terminated (Section 8.3), a multi-year term. Our only exit is cause-based: under Section 7.2(c) the Servicer may be removed solely if a Servicer Termination Event occurs and is continuing, and no at-will or convenience right exists anywhere for the Issuer or Depositor, who are the customer side here. The Optional Acquisition and Optional Redemption in Sections 8.1 and 8.2 are conditional Class A Certificateholder options (10% pool threshold; February 2021 date plus Make-Whole Payment; Administrator consent), not a customer convenience right. That is the walk-away case of no customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months, so the fallback is not met on its material terms. The Vendor side already exceeds both levels: Section 7.1 bars the Servicer from resigning except on legal inability, so that preferred element is already met and is left untouched (moving to the fallback would hand the Servicer an end-of-term convenience right it does not have). I therefore target preferred and insert only the missing customer convenience right, drafted as a new Section 7.2(e) removal reaching the Servicer's rights and obligations under this Agreement. Placing it inside Section 7.2 makes it a removal pursuant to that Section, so the Cellco reassumption in Section 7.2(c) and the Successor Servicer machinery in Section 7.4 engage, and it leaves the exhaustive Agreement-level termination triggers in Section 8.3 intact rather than contradicting them. Section 7.3 confirms effectiveness is the date stated in the notice of termination and is not conditioned on a Successor Servicer accepting engagement. Servicing Fees are payable in arrears on each Payment Date, so the refund limb is protective only.

mappings.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.

proposal.summary: Add Section 7.2(e) letting the Issuer, as customer, remove the Servicer for convenience on 30 days' notice with pro rata refund of prepaid Servicing Fees
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have no exit other than for a Servicer Termination Event, so we add a new Section 7.2(e) allowing us, as the customer, to remove the Servicer for convenience on thirty (30) days' written notice with a pro rata refund of any prepaid Servicing Fees. We have drafted it as a removal under Section 7.2 affecting the Servicer's rights and obligations only, so the Cellco reassumption, Continue to Perform and Successor Servicer mechanics engage and Section 8.3 is untouched; Section 7.1 already prevents the Servicer from walking away mid-term.

ops.text: (e) Termination for Convenience. The Issuer, as the customer under this Agreement, may, for convenience and without cause, remove the Servicer and terminate the Servicer's rights and obligations under this Agreement upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to the Servicer, and the Servicer will refund, pro rata, any Servicing Fees paid in advance for any period after the effective date of the termination.
